items.title: 5.8 Homogeneous Equation of the Second Degree in Two Variables (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 159 (PDF 161, upper part): pair of lines, joint equation (iii), general second degree equation (iv), lines y = m1 x, y = m2 x and their joint equation (v)

blocks.title: Ustad ki baat
blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Ab tak hum ek waqt mein ek hi straight line ki equation ke saath kaam karte aaye hain. Aaj ek naya aur dilchasp idea seekhenge: do lines ko mila kar sirf EK equation mein kaise likha jata hai. Is equation ko joint equation kehte hain. Sab se pehle hum yaad karte hain ke straight line ki equation hoti kaisi hai, phir dekhenge ke do equations ko multiply karne se kya banta hai, aur aakhir mein origin se guzarne wali do lines ki khaas equation tak pahunchenge. Yeh poori baat agle sections (5.8.1 aur 5.9) ki buniyaad hai, is liye ise aaraam se samajhiye.

Hum jaante hain ke agar kisi plane mein graph ek straight line ho, to us ki equation \(x\) aur \(y\) mein ek linear equation (pehle darje ki equation) hoti hai. Ulta bhi sach hai: \(x\) aur \(y\) mein har linear equation ka graph ek straight line hi hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Linear equation ka matlab hai degree 1 wali equation: har term ya to sirf number hai, ya number guna \(x\), ya number guna \(y\). Jaise \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\). Is mein \(x^{2}\), \(xy\) ya \(y^{2}\) jaisi koi cheez nahi hoti. Aisi equation hamesha seedhi line banati hai, aur har seedhi line ki aisi hi equation hoti hai. Is section mein hum DO lines ko EK equation mein jorenge, aur woh akeli equation degree 2 ki ban jayegi. Yahi is section ka asal khel hai.

Farz karein humare paas do straight lines hain jin ki equations yeh hain:
\[a_{1}x + b_{1}y + c_{1} = 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
aur
\[a_{2}x + b_{2}y + c_{2} = 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]

Ab equations (i) aur (ii) ke left sides ko aapas mein multiply karte hain aur result ko zero ke barabar rakhte hain:
\[(a_{1}x + b_{1}y + c_{1})\times\]
\[(a_{2}x + b_{2}y + c_{2}) = 0 \quad \text{...(iii)}\]
Yeh \(x\) aur \(y\) mein second degree (doosre darje) ki equation hai, kyunke ek bracket ka \(x\) doosre bracket ke \(x\) se multiply ho kar \(x^{2}\) bana deta hai.

Equation (iii) ko lines (i) aur (ii) ki joint equation of the pair of lines (lines ke jore ki mushtarka equation) kehte hain. Doosri taraf, agar humein \(x\) aur \(y\) mein second degree ki koi equation di jaye, maslan
\[ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2}\]
\[+\, 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 \quad \text{...(iv)}\]
jahan \(a \ne 0\), to yeh lines ke ek jore ko tabhi represent karti hai jab (iv) ko do linear factors (pehle darje ke hisson) mein tor kar likha ja sake. Is section mein hum un khaas joint equations ko parhenge jin ki dono lines origin se guzarti hain.
bold: joint equation of the pair of lines

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Multiply karne se kaam kyun chalta hai? Zero-product rule yaad kijiye: do cheezon ka product tabhi zero hota hai jab un mein se kam az kam ek zero ho. Is liye koi point \((x, y)\) equation (iii) ko tabhi satisfy karega jab woh (i) ko satisfy kare ya (ii) ko, yani jab woh do mein se kisi ek line par para ho. Is tarah ek hi equation dono lines ko ek saath bayan kar deti hai. Isi liye ise 'joint' (mushtarka) equation kehte hain.
Degree 2 kyun? Har bracket degree 1 ka hai. Jab \(x\) wala term doosre \(x\) wale term se multiply ho to \(x^{2}\), \(x\) aur \(y\) multiply hon to \(xy\), aur \(y\) aur \(y\) se \(y^{2}\) banta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Lines \(x - y = 0\) aur \(x + y = 0\) lijiye. Pehli line par har point ka \(y\) us ke \(x\) ke barabar hai, doosri par \(y = -x\). In ki joint equation:
\[(x - y)(x + y) = 0\]
\[x^{2} - y^{2} = 0\]
Ab check kijiye: point \((2, 2)\) pehli line par hai; \(4 - 4 = 0\), haan joint equation bhi satisfy hui. Point \((3, -3)\) doosri line par hai; \(9 - 9 = 0\), yeh bhi theek. Lekin \((1, 2)\) kisi line par nahi; \(1 - 4 = -3 \ne 0\). Dekha? Joint equation sirf unhi points ko qubool karti hai jo dono mein se kisi line par hon.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ulti taraf dhyan se chalna hai: har second degree equation lines ka jora nahi hoti. Maslan \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 1 = 0\) ek circle hai; ise real coefficients wale do linear factors mein tora hi nahi ja sakta. Isi liye kitab kehti hai ke (iv) sirf tab lines ka jora hai JAB woh do linear factors mein resolve ho sake.
Equation (iv) mein beech wala term \(2hxy\) likha gaya hai (aur \(2gx\), \(2fy\) bhi), yani aage 2 laga hua hai. Yeh sirf ek riwaaj (convention) hai jis se aage ke formulas saaf aur chhote ban jate hain, jaise Theorem 8 mein \(h^{2} - ab\). Is liye sawal mein \(xy\) ka coefficient dekh kar hamesha us ka aadha \(h\) lena hai.

Ab farz karein \(y = m_{1}x\) aur \(y = m_{2}x\) do lines hain jo dono origin se guzarti hain (in mein constant term nahi, is liye \(x = 0\) par \(y = 0\)). In ki joint equation yeh hai:
\[(y - m_{1}x)(y - m_{2}x) = 0\]
ya
\[y^{2} - (m_{1}+m_{2})xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2} = 0 \quad \text{...(v)}\]
Equation (v) ek second degree homogeneous equation (aisi equation jis ke har term ki degree barabar ho) ki ek khaas qisam hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Equation (v) kaise bani? Brackets ko step by step kholte hain:
\[(y - m_{1}x)(y - m_{2}x)\]
\[= y^{2} - m_{2}xy - m_{1}xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}\]
\[= y^{2} - (m_{1}+m_{2})xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}\]
Beech ke do terms mein \(xy\) common tha, us ko bahar nikal kar \(-(m_{1}+m_{2})xy\) likha.
Ab (v) ko ghaur se dekhiye: har term ki total degree bilkul 2 hai (\(y^{2}\), \(xy\), \(x^{2}\)). Akela \(x\) wala term nahi, akela \(y\) wala term nahi, aur koi constant bhi nahi. 'Homogeneous' ka yahi matlab hai. Aur yeh is liye hua ke dono lines origin se guzarti hain: \(x = 0, y = 0\) rakhne par jawab zero aana hi chahiye.
Ek aur kaam ki baat: jab \(y^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 ho, to \(xy\) ka coefficient slopes ke JAMA ka minus hai aur \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient slopes ka PRODUCT hai. Yeh baat hum 5.9 mein angle nikalne ke liye istemal karenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Lines \(y = 2x\) aur \(y = -3x\) ki joint equation kya hogi? Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir neeche dekhiye.
Jawab: \((y - 2x)(y + 3x) = 0\), yani \(y^{2} + xy - 6x^{2} = 0\). Check: slopes ka jama \(2 + (-3) = -1\), is ka minus \(+1\) = \(xy\) ka coefficient; product \(-6\) = \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient. Bilkul (v) ke mutabiq.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Do lines ki joint equation = dono equations ka product, zero ke barabar.
2. Do linear equations ka product \(x\) aur \(y\) mein second degree equation banata hai.
3. Second degree equation (iv) lines ka jora tabhi hai jab woh do linear factors mein toot sake; warna woh circle wagaira bhi ho sakti hai.
4. Origin se guzarne wali lines \(y = m_{1}x\), \(y = m_{2}x\) ki joint equation (v) hai, jis ka har term degree 2 ka hai (homogeneous).
5. \(y^{2}\) ka coefficient 1 ho to: \(xy\) ka coefficient \(= -(m_{1}+m_{2})\), \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient \(= m_{1}m_{2}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Equations ko multiply karne ke bajaye jama kar dena. \((x - y) + (x + y) = 0\) se \(x = 0\) banta hai, jo sirf ek line hai, jora nahi. Dono lines sirf product mein bachti hain.
2. Yeh samajhna ke har second degree equation lines ka jora hai. \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 1\) circle hai.
3. Bracket kholte waqt beech ke do \(xy\) terms mein se ek bhool jana; hamesha chaar products banate hain.
